data.one_liner: CLI for AI agents to interact with running Flutter apps on device.
data.what_it_does: Provides a terminal CLI for AI coding agents and developers to launch, hot reload, screenshot, inspect the widget tree, filter logs, and interact with running Flutter apps on real devices and simulators.
use_when: You want an AI agent to see, run, and test your Flutter app on a real device or simulator via bash commands
You need to take screenshots, hot reload, and inspect widget trees programmatically from the terminal
avoid_when: You are looking for code analysis, package management, or static code assistance (use the official Flutter MCP server instead)
strengths: Works with any AI agent or environment that can run bash commands
Requires zero dependencies in the Flutter app itself for basic tasks
Enables end-to-end device interaction including screenshots, tapping, and hot reloading
weaknesses: Some advanced widget-targeted commands require the optional fdb_helper
Physical iOS and desktop targets have limited or unsupported native interaction features
data.setup_notes: Run 'dart pub global activate fdb' and ensure ~/.pub-cache/bin is in your PATH.
data.minimal_example:
fdb launch --device <device_id> --project /path/to/app
fdb screenshot
fdb reload
